description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

The Future of Work Fund (FWF) is an innovative blended finance vehicle that combines catalytic equity, impact debt, and stakeholder investments to prove that a fair, ethical student finance solution can truly serve marginalised youth as well as function sustainably across regions in Sub-Saharan Africa. The FWF intends to serve as an impact orientated refinancing vehicle of loans, specifically using the Income Share Agreement (ISA) model to finance tuition fees for excluded youth in partnership with selected higher education institutions. Using the ISA financial instrument tested by Chancen over 25 years, the FWF aims to create a paradigm shift in education to employment across the continent. The fund will provide student financing for 10.000 youths, with a specific focus on women and other traditionally excluded populations in Rwanda, South Africa and Kenya.

description.narrative: (Rwanda): Building on recent investments in civil society development and rule of law programs, USAID, via the Access to Justice activity, will use FY 2018 funds to increase access to justice and enhance the rule of law in Rwanda. The Access to Justice activity will improve justice services through its consortia of local civil society organizations. The activity takes a two-part approach to help Rwanda improve conditions for durable peace and development through strengthened democratic processes (USAID, CDCS Development Objective #2). First, it will improve the effectiveness of court mechanisms (formal and traditional mechanisms) and second, it will improve public understanding of and access to judicial system processes and legal rights. An improved judiciary will be achieved by training for judges on substantive issues and professionalism as well as on using the integrated case electronic management system (IECMS) in order to improve adherence to the law and enhance critical thinking of legal professionals. Further, the activity will enhance effectiveness of the community-based justice system, the Abunzi (traditional courts), local mediators, lawyers, paralegals, and others through training and capacity building. The Access to Justice activity will address the demand side of judicial accountability by helping to cultivate an informed public who seek effective, accessible dispute resolution through outreach and citizen education. Ultimately the activity works towards improved judicial effectiveness, a more independent judiciary capable of providing checks to a powerful Executive, promotion of community-level dispute resolution, and a better-informed public. With better and stronger systems in place and better judicial education for all, Rwandans will be better prepared to advocate for their own rights, and better able to hold their government accountable to the rule of law.

description.narrative: (Rwanda): The Integrated Improved Livelihood Program (IILP) aims to improve the livelihoods and food consumption of Rwanda's very poor, particularly women, by building sustainable linkages to financial services, inputs, markets and information - all of which serve as key enabling factors for increased economic opportunities in rural areas. In addition, IILP implements complementary short-term and long-term interventions to ensure that most vulnerable populations are supported in a way that allows them to attain critical skills and knowledge, leading to greater food security and a better understanding of the relationship between diet, nutrition and hygiene. With FY 2014 funds, IILP's activities will include the transfer of agricultural technologies, promotion of functional literacy and financial education programs, and support to community-based savings and lending groups and nutrition groups. Particular focus will be on the scaling up of the cultivation and consumption of iron-fortified beans by farmers and rural households. IILP will also assist micro-, small-, and medium-enterprises to access loans through local microfinance institutions.

(Rwanda): USAID's Rwanda Dairy Sector Competitiveness Project II (RDCP II) works with smallholder dairy producers to improve milk quality, reduce transaction costs, and increase investments along the dairy value chain. ~RDCP II activities will reduce poverty by expanding the production and marketing of quality milk, which generates income and employment, and improves the nutrition of rural households. ~With FY 2015 funding, USAID will expand a national milk consumption campaign and build the management capacity of ~milk producing cooperatives. ~The program will help to scale up technologies that enable the adoption of artificial insemination, disease management, and best management practices in animal husbandry. ~USAID will support Government of Rwanda (GOR) agencies to implement an inspection and certification program for dairy products and to build the capacity of the Rwanda National Dairy Platform, an association of dairy sector players that advocates on behalf of members on policy issues and strengthens members' capacity for market expansion.

(Rwanda): USAID's Gimbuka (Be Resilient) Program supports Rwanda's efforts to address chronic malnutrition. With FY 2018 funds, USAID through Caritas Rwanda will improve the nutritional status of women and children, especially those under two years in Ruhango district and select administrative sectors in eight other districts, through community-based nutrition behavior change interventions. The funding will address issues around poor complementary feeding practices among children under five years of age and pregnant lactating women. This will be achieved through a positive deviance hearth model, where caretakers of well-nourished children will mentor families with moderately malnourished children to adopt healthy feeding practices and dietary diversity. Gimbuka will reach a total of 89,681 children under five with growth monitoring and promotion, and implement water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) interventions (e.g. handwashing, safe water use, latrine cleanliness) to prevent diarrheal diseases. With Maternal and Child Health (MCH) funds, Gimbuka will promote maternal health by encouraging pregnant women to attend at least four antenatal care visits at health facilities, and providing nutrition counseling and cooking demonstration lessons to promote a healthy and safe pregnancy. .Gimbuka's community-based approach ensures USAID reaches the most vulnerable women and children, empowering them to adopt healthier feeding and improved sanitation practices. Gimbuka directly contributes to the Country Development Cooperation Strategy (CDCS) goal of improving the health and nutrition status of Rwandans. ..

(Rwanda): Through the Turengere Abana (Let us protect the children) activity, USAID supports an integrated approach in seven districts to improve the wellbeing of orphans, vulnerable children and their families, especially those affected by HIV/AIDS. With FY 2018 funds, USAID will reach a total of 42,000 children under five with growth monitoring and promotion, and provide their mothers and caretakers with nutritional education and counseling. FY 2018 funding will be used to improve complementary feeding practices among children under five years of age and pregnant lactating women, and to promote WASH activities, including hand washing, safe water use, and latrine cleanliness to prevent diarrheal diseases among children. With MCH funds, Turengere Abana will promote safe pregnancies by encouraging pregnant women to attend at least four antenatal care visits at health facilities and providing nutrition counseling and cooking demonstrations to increase weight gain..Turengere Abana is implemented by FXB Rwanda, a local partner with strong expertise in improving the well being of orphans, vulnerable children and their families. description.narrative: (Rwanda): Isuku Iwacu (Hygiene in our Area) is working with the private sector to increase the availability of sanitary and hygiene products and using social behavior change communications (SBCC) to encourage greater use of these products and improve hygiene practices. It is working with local construction companies and retail sellers of sanitation products to expand the market for sanitation products, by providing training on business development services and data management activities, and also providing technical assistance to private sector led, government supported district sanitation centers to help them improve their marketing of sanitary and hygiene products, and providing business development skills to improve the operation of these public private partnerships. Isuku Iwacu will also work with Microfinance Institutions to design sanitation loans to enable Rwandans and businesses to more easily purchase needed sanitary products..Through SBCC in eight districts, Isuku Iwacu will promote hand washing, safe water use, latrine cleanliness and the elimination of open defecation in order to prevent diarrheal diseases among children. Isuku Iwacu will continue to disseminate National Sanitation Policies and Strategy and its communication materials and support the Ministry of Infrastructure to conduct a Water and Sanitation sector analysis. Isuku Iwacu compliments other USAID nutrition activities by increasing the availability of sanitation and hygiene products in order to respond to the demand for sanitation products being generated by these other activities..The implementing partner for Isuku Iwacu, SNV USA, has significant experience and technical expertise in advancing child health through WASH programming. Isuku Iwacu support for improved sanitary and hygiene outcomes supports the Embassy's Integrated Country Strategy objective 3.1 to improve the health and nutritional status of Rwandans, and thereby Mission Goal 3, to promote inclusive country-led development..
